findings.diagnosis: The prompt underrates cuts immediately after sentence‑initial single‑word grammatical prefaces (discourse markers, determiners, short subordinators/auxiliaries), causing longer initial fragments that harm short‑latency bins.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_956','en_us_1543','en_us_535','en_us_553','en_us_651','en_us_784','en_us_1615'] — these 7 cases all show the offline target adding an early cut that isolates a one‑word or very short grammatical preface (The / In / If / So / Perhaps / introductory adverbial) from the following resolved NP or clause.
findings.type_predicate: Sentence begins with a single short grammatical preface (one word or a 1–2 word discourse/subordinating/auxiliary token) immediately followed by the main noun phrase or clause.

edit.text: If a sentence starts with a lone short grammatical preface (single determiner, discourse marker, subordinating word or auxiliary), prefer a cut immediately after it so the following piece contains the resolved NP or predicate.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt fails to prefer cuts immediately after closed parentheticals or parenthetical dates/identifiers, leaving the following clause unresolved and reducing cohesion.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_1179','en_us_685'] — these 2 cases both show the offline target inserting a cut right after a parenthetical (date/identifier) so the next segment begins with the main clause/verb rather than a continuation of the parenthetical.
findings.type_predicate: A parenthetical expression (text in parentheses or an immediate parenthetical identifier) ends before a continuing clause or main verb.
